o: A prefix of s is a residue when its number of distinct characters equals its length mod 3. In "abc", prefixes "a" (1 distinct, 1%3) and "ab" (2 distinct, 2%3) qualify, giving 2; in "dd" only "d" qualifies; "bob" gives 2. With length <= 100, even recomputing the distinct set per prefix works, but a single scan maintaining a growing set answers in O(n).
k: Distinct count only grows as the prefix extends, so one running set suffices.
The condition compares len % 3 with the set size - both O(1) once the set is maintained.
Non-empty prefixes only, so iterate over all lengths 1..n.

a.i: For each prefix length, build the set of characters in s[0..i] and compare its size to (i+1) % 3. Perfectly adequate for n <= 100.
s: For i from 0 to n-1, form set(s[:i+1]).
If its size equals (i+1) % 3, increment the answer.
a.t: O(n^2) - each prefix rebuilds its character set

a.i: Extend a persistent set one character at a time; the distinct count never decreases, so no rebuilding is needed.
s: Maintain a set and a counter over the scan.
At each index add the character, then test setSize == (index+1) % 3.
a.t: O(n) - one pass with O(1) amortized set updates
a.sp: O(1) - the set holds at most 26 letters

w: Show the one-liner scan; the brute force is only to demonstrate the definition. Pitfalls: comparing with length instead of length mod 3, and forgetting prefixes are non-empty (start the modulus check at length 1, where len%3 = 1). Follow-up: count residue suffixes, or generalize the modulus.
